content:
If you've recently purchased a new Mac, such as the newly released Mac mini or Mac Studio, you might be looking to add an external display.

Here are my recommendations, covering multiple product categories, price ranges, and other considerations.

Best external displays for Mac

Apple Studio Display

When it comes to the best displays on the market, Apple's Studio Display is a must-mention. Although it's on the pricey side, it features Apple's signature outstanding design, with a 27-inch 5K display.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 ppi
  • Brightness: 600 nits
  • Color support: Wide color gamut (P3), supporting 1 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: 12-megapixel Center Stage camera, supporting Desk View
  • True Tone technology: Automatically adjusts display color temperature to match ambient light
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports (up to 120Gb/s) and two USB-C ports (up to 10Gb/s)
  • Host charging: Up to 96W

The Studio Display comes in multiple configurations at different price points, which I'll list below. If you want an iMac-like experience with your Mac, the Apple Studio Display is the only choice.

Standard glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Standard glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Apple Studio Display XDR

The Studio Display XDR launched earlier this year and offers several major advantages over the standard Studio Display, including mini-LED display technology and a 120Hz refresh rate.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina XDR display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 ppi, with mini-LED backlighting and 2,304 local dimming zones
  • Brightness: Up to 1,000 nits SDR, up to 2,000 nits peak HDR
  • Color support: P3 and Adobe RGB wide color gamut, supporting 1 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 120Hz with Adaptive Sync
  • Host charging: Up to 140W

Of course, these advantages come at a higher price, making it more expensive than the standard Studio Display.

Samsung M9 Smart Monitor

The 32-inch Samsung M9 Smart Monitor is a fairly attractive option for Mac users, featuring a 4K OLED panel. My 9to5Toys colleague Justin Kahn, after switching to this display, said "the past few months pairing it with my Mac mini have been a real pleasure."

  • Panel: 32-inch 4K OLED display (3840×2160 resolution) with anti-glare coating
  • Refresh rate: 165Hz
  • Ports: DisplayPort, HDMI, USB-C, 2 USB-A
  • Built-in camera: Yes, 4K
  • HDR support: Yes (HDR10/HDR10+)

Although its resolution can't match some 5K or 6K models, you'll enjoy all the benefits of OLED, including deeper blacks, better color reproduction, and contrast.

Buy the Samsung M9 OLED Smart Monitor:

LG UltraFine 6K

The LG UltraFine 6K is an evolution of LG's high-end display business. It features a 32-inch panel with a resolution of 6144 x 3456 pixels and plenty of ports. Here are the key specs:

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K Nano IPS Black display (6144×3456 resolution), 224 ppi
  • Brightness: 450 nits typical; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 98% DCI-P3 and 99.5% Adobe RGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • True Tone: None; supports auto brightness adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports, one DisplayPort 2.1, one HDMI 2.1, two downstream USB-C ports, and one upstream USB-C port
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt
  • Contrast ratio: 2,000:1

LG UltraFine 6K purchase link:

Asus ProArt 5K Display

My colleague Jeff Benjamin got hands-on with this monitor, and it immediately caught my attention. The Asus ProArt (PA27JCV) 5K display offers the same 5K resolution (5120×2880) and the same 27-inch size, but at half the price of the Studio Display.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 ppi
  • Brightness: 400 nits typical; VESA DisplayHDR 500 certified
  • Color support: 99% DCI-P3, 100% sRGB, and 95% Adobe RGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz with Adaptive-Sync
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient light adjustment: Ambient light and backlight sensors automatically adjust brightness and color temperature
  • Ports: One USB-C supporting DisplayPort Alt Mode, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, three USB-A, one downstream USB-C, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via USB-C

Above is Jeff's full review with all the details. If you want a 5K display for your Mac, the Asus ProArt is hard to beat.

Asus ProArt 5K display purchase link:

Asus ProArt 6K Display

If you're looking for a larger, higher-resolution display, Asus has you covered. The new Asus ProArt 6K display (PA32QCV) is a 32-inch monitor with a native resolution of 6016 x 3384. Jeff called it "incredible value for money" in his review.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K IPS display (6016×3384 resolution), 218 ppi
  • Brightness: 400 nits typical, 600 nits HDR peak; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 98% DCI-P3 and 100% sRGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz with Adaptive-Sync (48–60Hz)
  • Camera: None
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, USB-C and USB-A hub, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt 4

Perhaps the most appealing aspect of the Asus ProArt 6K display is its price. It's significantly cheaper than some of the most popular 4K and 5K displays on the market.

Asus ProArt 6K display purchase link:

Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K (S80HF)

Samsung's ViewFinity S8 5K is another attractive option to pair with your new Mac, offering 5K resolution.

  • Brightness: 350 nits typical
  • Color support: 99% sRGB, supporting 1.07 billion colors; HDR10
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient light adjustment: Adaptive Picture automatically adjusts brightness based on ambient light
  • Ports: One USB-C port with 90W power delivery, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-A ports, one downstream USB-C port, Ethernet, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 90W via USB-C

Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K purchase link:

BenQ 27-inch 5K PD2730S Thunderbolt Monitor

This might be my current favorite choice. The BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K monitor comes packed with Mac-friendly features, and of course, the headliner is its crisp 5K resolution.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 ppi, with Nano Matte coating
  • Brightness: 400 nits typical and peak; VESA DisplayHDR 400 certified
  • Color support: 100% sRGB, 100% Rec.709, and 98% P3, supporting 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ports: One upstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one downstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one upstream USB-C port, one downstream USB-C port, three USB-A ports, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 90W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Hotkey Puck G3: Physical external controller supporting custom operations

BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K monitor purchase link:

Read our full review: BenQ's 27-inch 5K Thunderbolt 4 designer display is a true competitor to the Apple Studio Display

BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt Monitor

If you're looking for a 32-inch display for your new Mac priced under $1,000, this is one of the most attractive options. The biggest downside is that you "only" get 4K resolution instead of 5K. But it has a wide range of port options, and the 32-inch panel costs less than $1,000.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 4K IPS Black display (3840×2160 resolution), 140 ppi
  • Color support: 98% P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, supporting 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient light adjustment: No automatic ambient light color temperature adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 3 ports, two HDMI 2.0 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one downstream USB-C port, three USB-A ports, USB-B, and one headphone jack
  • Host charging: Up to 85W via Thunderbolt 3

BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt monitor purchase link:

Read our full review: Is a 32-inch 4K Mac monitor really not worth considering?

Dell U4025QW 40-inch Ultrawide Monitor

If you want to pair your Mac with an ultrawide monitor, the Dell U4025QW is one of the best options on the market. It combines 5K resolution and a 120Hz refresh rate in a 40-inch display. Plus, it has plenty of ports, a matte screen, and more.

  • Display: 39.7-inch curved 5K2K IPS Black display (5120×2160 resolution), 140 ppi, 21:9 aspect ratio, 2500R curvature
  • Brightness: 450 nits typical, 600 nits HDR peak; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color support: 99% DCI-P3, 99% Display P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, supporting 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh rate: Up to 120Hz with VRR support
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient light adjustment: Ambient light sensor automatically adjusts brightness and color temperature
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-C ports, five USB-A ports, 2.5Gb Ethernet, and audio output
  • Host charging: Up to 140W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Speakers: Two 9W speakers

Dell U4025QW 40-inch ultrawide monitor purchase link:

Samsung ViewFinity S65TC

If you want a more affordable way to enter the ultrawide monitor market, the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC is an option, currently available at nearly half off. Although it doesn't have as many features as other models, you still get a 34-inch ultrawide curved display and plenty of ports, including a Thunderbolt 4 port with power delivery support.

  • Display: 34-inch ultrawide curved display, Ultra-WQHD resolution (3440×1440), 1000R curvature, offering an immersive viewing experience.
  • Brightness: 350 nits typical.
  • Camera: None.
  • Ports: One Thunderbolt 4 port (providing up to 90W power delivery), one HDMI 2.0 port, one DisplayPort 1.2, three USB-A 3.0 ports, one RJ45 Ethernet port, and one 3.5mm headphone jack.

Samsung ViewFinity S65TC purchase link:

Conclusion

These are just some of the best external display options to pair with your new Mac. They all offer excellent macOS integration, rich connectivity options, and unique sizes and designs.

Did you recently buy a new Mac? Which display are you using to pair with it? Feel free to share with us in the comments.
